title: Chapter 34. Nagari Padas — VIII: Lochana Dasa (22 padas from GPT, sect. 3.2, nos. 62–85, 116); concluding note to the section of nagari padas
html:
On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27.

Chapter 34 is the last of the section of nagari padas: the padas signed by Lochana Dasa in section 3.2 of the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT). There are 26 of them: nos. 61–85 (GPT1 pp. 177–189, scan PDF pp. 436–448, in one continuous block) and no. 116 (p. 204, PDF p. 463). All have been checked against the scan of GPT1 (text and signatures), against GPT2 (same numbering, same text), the Padakalpataru (PK), the Padamrita-samudra, the Kshanada-gita-chintamani, Lochana's Chaitanya-mangala (our translation) and the anthologies of the early twentieth century. Four padas are not translated anew here: no. 61 "nadīyā-nāgarī sāri sāri sāri…" = PK 2178 and no. 66 "āra śunecha ālo sai…" = PK 2174 were translated in chapter 28 (nos. 28 and 27); no. 80 "ānanda nadīyāpure ṭalamala premabhare…" = PK 2088 is a passage of the Chaitanya-mangala itself (Madhya-khanda: the Lord in kirtana, raga sindhura, with the refrain "The town of Nadia rejoices…"; our translation — Chaitanya-mangala, Madhya-khanda, part 4, vv. 110–118; GPT gives vv. 110–114 and 118, without vv. 115–117), in content a praise of the Lord in kirtana, not nagari-bhava; no. 84 "nirabadhi gorārūpa mane jāgiyāche go…" = PK 777, signed by Vasu Ghosha (translated in chapter 27, no. 16): in GPT1 the same pada also stands as no. 17 with Vasu's signature, so Lochana's signature in no. 84 contradicts both PK and GPT itself. The remaining 22 padas are translated below (nos. 1–22).

Lochana Dasa (c. 1520 — ?) is the author of the Chaitanya-mangala, a disciple of Narahari Sarakara Thakura of Shrikhanda, a younger contemporary of the Lord's associates; he himself did not see the Lord. The nagari motif is present in the Chaitanya-mangala too (the women of Nadia, forgetting shame, hurry to look at Gaura — see our translation, Chaitanya-mangala, Adi-khanda, part 1, note 9; Chaitanya-mangala, Adi-khanda, part 10, notes 5–6); Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati, publishing the Chaitanya-mangala (1922), refuses in his preface to ascribe to it "the doctrine of gaura-nagari" (the translator's preface to our translation of the Chaitanya-mangala). The padas of this chapter are of two kinds: (1) padas in the literary language of the padas, in payar and tripadi metre (nos. 1–4, 15–17, 21); (2) padas in colloquial Bengali, in short rhymed feet, with colloquial forms ("dekhalāma", "halo", "ka're") and kirtana singers' insertions in brackets (nos. 5–14, 18–20, 22) — in the manner of the playful songs traditionally connected with Lochana's name (dhāmālī, "dhamali"). The padas of the second kind are known only from GPT (two of them — nos. 16, 17 — are also in the anthology Prachina-vaishnava-padavali, 1922, with Lochana's signature); their language was probably renewed in oral transmission. None of the 22 padas is in PK or in the Chaitanya-mangala; Lochana's signature does not compete with any other (except in no. 84, excluded above). The attribution rests only on the signature in GPT: Lochana is a recognized author, but these padas have no independent witnesses (PVP, 1922, is a late anthology), hence C ("attribution by GPT only"; cf. Lochana's padas from PK in chapter 28 — B). Where a pada builds on someone else's lines (no. 5 begins with two couplets of Jnanadasa's pada PK 748), this is noted.

The translation is faithful to the author, without worldly vocabulary beyond the original and without softening: where a townswoman speaks of attraction, embraces, a dream, it is translated exactly, with a note on the position of the tradition. The Bengali text, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book. At the end — the summary of the chapter and the concluding note to the whole section of nagari padas (chapters 27–34).

1. Lochana Dasa — "gaurāṅga-taraṅge nayana majila…" (GPT1 pp. 177–178, no. 62)

Nagari-bhava. The townswoman's eyes have drowned in the waves of Gauranga: she is ready to take disgrace upon herself and leave home; all her household work betrays her — she knows nothing but Gora, in anyone she meets she sees Gauranga; lying with her husband, she imagines Gaurahari coming and taking her to Himself. Raga pahida.1

গৌরাঙ্গ-তরঙ্গে নয়ন মজিল কিবা সে করিব সার ।
কলঙ্কের ডালি মাথায় ধরিয়া ঘরে না রহিব আর ॥

gaurāṅga-taraṅge nayana majila kibā se kariba sāra |
kalaṅkera ḍāli māthāya dhariyā ghare nā rahiba āra ||

gaurāṅga-taraṅge — in the waves of Gauranga; nayana majila — the eyes have drowned; kibā se kariba sāra — what shall I make my all; kalaṅkera ḍāli — the basket of disgrace; māthāya dhariyā — holding on the head; ghare nā rahiba āra — I will stay at home no more

1.1In the waves of Gauranga my eyes have drowned — what now shall I choose?
Lifting the basket of disgrace onto my head, I will stay at home no more.

সই এবে সে করিব কি ।
গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের নিছনি লইয়া গৃহে সমাধান দি ॥

sai ebe se kariba ki |
gaurāṅgacām̐dera nichani laiyā gṛhe samādhāna di ||

sai — friend; ebe se kariba ki — what am I to do now; gaurāṅgacām̐dera nichani laiyā — giving myself away (nichani) for Gaurangachand; gṛhe samādhāna di — I make an end of the house

1.2(Refrain) Friend, what am I to do now?
Giving myself away for Gaurangachand, I will make an end of the house.2

গৃহধর্ম্ম যত হইল বেকত গোরা বিনা নাহি জানি ।
আনেরে দেখিয়া ভরমে ভুলিয়া গৌরাঙ্গ বলি যে আমি ॥

gṛhadharmma yata haila bekata gorā binā nāhi jāni |
ānere dekhiyā bharame bhuliyā gaurāṅga bali ye āmi ||

gṛha-dharmma yata — all the household duties; haila bekata — it became manifest; gorā binā nāhi jāni — I know nothing but Gora; ānere dekhiyā — seeing another; bharame bhuliyā — mistaken in confusion; gaurāṅga bali ye āmi — I say "Gauranga"

1.3All my household work — it is plain to everyone now: I know nothing but Gora;
seeing another, mistaking him in my confusion, I say: "Gauranga!"

পতির সহিতে শুতিয়া থাকিতে গৌরাঙ্গ জাগয়ে মনে ।
আসি তরাতরি প্রাণ গৌরহরি পতিরে ফেলাঞা ভূমে ॥

patira sahite śutiyā thākite gaurāṅga jāgaye mane |
āsi tarātari prāṇa gaurahari patire phelāñā bhūme ||

patira sahite — with the husband; śutiyā thākite — while lying; gaurāṅga jāgaye mane — Gauranga awakens in the heart; āsi tarātari — coming in haste; prāṇa gaurahari — Gaurahari, [my] life; patire phelāñā bhūme — throwing the husband to the ground

1.4When I lie with my husband, Gauranga awakens in my heart:
Gaurahari, my life, comes in haste and throws my husband down on the ground;

আমারে লইয়া করে উরপরে বদনে বদন দিয়া ।
আবেশে গৌরাঙ্গ সুধা উগারয়ে প্রতি অঙ্গে পড়ে বাইঞা ॥

āmāre laiyā kare urapare badane badana diyā |
ābeśe gaurāṅga sudhā ugāraye prati aṅge paṛe bāiñā ||

āmāre laiyā — taking me; kare ura-pare — places on the breast; badane badana diyā — pressing face to face; ābeśe gaurāṅga — Gauranga in ecstasy; sudhā ugāraye — pours out nectar; prati aṅge paṛe bāiñā — it flows down over every limb

1.5He takes me, places me on His breast, presses face to face;
in ecstasy Gauranga pours out nectar — it flows down over every limb.3

গৌরাঙ্গ-রতন করিয়া যতন মোড়াঞা লইব কোলে ।
তিলাঞ্জলি দিয়া সকলি ভাসানু এ দাস লোচন বলে ॥

gaurāṅga-ratana kariyā yatana moṛāñā laiba kole |
tilāñjali diyā sakali bhāsānu e dāsa locana bale ||

gaurāṅga-ratana — Gauranga the jewel; kariyā yatana — carefully; moṛāñā laiba kole — I will enfold in my arms; tilāñjali diyā — bidding farewell for ever; sakali bhāsānu — I let everything float away; e dāsa locana bale — says this servant Lochana

1.6Gauranga, the jewel, I will carefully enfold in my arms;
bidding farewell to all, I have let everything float away, — says this servant Lochana.4

(same text). The pada is not in PK, the Padamrita-samudra, KGC or the Chaitanya-mangala; no other witnesses have been found. On Lochana Dasa see chapter 28, note 75, and the note at the beginning of this chapter: a disciple of Narahari Sarakara, a younger contemporary of the Lord's associates; attribution by GPT only — C. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). away for Gaurangachand" (nichani laiyā) — the nichhani rite (chapter 27, note 10). "I will make an end of the house" (gṛhe samādhāna di) — lit. "I will give the house its conclusion." as in the original, without softening. This is precisely the notion of Gaura as the lover of the townswomen ("gaura-nagari") which the Gaudiya tradition rejects: according to the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi-khanda), the Lord in this incarnation did not look at any woman; Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati counts "gaura-nagari" among the apasampradayas (introductory note). According to Majumdar, nagari padas known only from GPT are an unreliable and late layer. "Pours out nectar" (sudhā ugāraye) is an image of sweetness common in padas on Krishna. let float away" (bhāsānu) is in the past tense, while "I will enfold" (laiba) is in the future; so in the original.

2. Lochana Dasa — "śuna śuna sai āra kichu kai…" (GPT1 p. 178, no. 63)

Nagari-bhava. "Listen, friend: Gauranga is not a man!" Ever since the townswoman saw the moon of His face, her eyes have drowned in the ocean of beauty; at the ghat and in the field she sees Gora, the colour of a golden filament; sitting among the elders, she remembers His face; giving herself away for Him, she will leave everything. Raga kamoda.5

শুন শুন সই আর কিছু কই গৌরাঙ্গ মানুষ নয় ।
ভুবন মাঝারে শচীর কুমারে উপমা কিসে বা হয় ॥

śuna śuna sai āra kichu kai gaurāṅga mānuṣa naya |
bhubana mājhāre śacīra kumāre upamā kise bā haya ||

śuna śuna sai — listen, listen, friend; āra kichu kai — I tell you more; gaurāṅga mānuṣa naya — Gauranga is not a man; bhubana mājhāre — in the world; śacīra kumāre — for the son of Shachi; upamā kise vā haya — what comparison can there be

2.1Listen, listen, friend, I will tell you more: Gauranga is not a man!
In all the world, to what can the son of Shachi be compared?6

ছাড়িতে না পারি যে অবধি হেরি গৌরাঙ্গবদনচাঁদ ।
সে রূপসায়রে নয়ান ডুবিল লাগিল পীরিতি ফাঁদ ॥

chāṛite nā pāri ye abadhi heri gaurāṅgabadanacām̐da |
se rūpasāyare nayāna ḍubila lāgila pīriti phām̐da ||

chāṛite nā pāri — I cannot leave; ye abadhi heri — since I saw; gaurāṅga-badana-cām̐da — the moon of Gauranga's face; se rūpa-sāyare — in that ocean of beauty; nayāna ḍubila — the eyes drowned; lāgila pīriti phām̐da — the noose of love caught

2.2Since I saw the moon of Gauranga's face, I cannot turn away [from it]:
in that ocean of beauty my eyes have drowned, the noose of love has tightened.

ঘাটে মাঠে যাই হেরি গো সদাই কনক-কেশর গোরা ।
কুলের বিচার ধরম আচার সকলি করিল ছাড়া ॥

ghāṭe māṭhe yāi heri go sadāi kanaka-keśara gorā |
kulera bicāra dharama ācāra sakali karila chāṛā ||

ghāṭe māṭhe yāi — I go to the ghat, to the field; heri go sadāi — I see all the time; kanaka-keśara gorā — Gora, the golden filament; kulera bicāra — the honour (judgement) of family; dharama ācāra — dharma and custom; sakali karila chāṛā — He made me give it all up

2.3Whether I go to the ghat or the field — I see Gora all the time, the golden filament;
the honour of family, dharma and custom — all this He has made me leave.7

থাকি গুরু মাঝে হেরি গো নয়নে বয়ান পড়িছে মনে ।
নিবারিতে চাই নাহি নিবারণ বিকল করিল প্রাণে ॥

thāki guru mājhe heri go nayane bayāna paṛiche mane |
nibārite cāi nāhi nibāraṇa bikala karila prāṇe ||

thāki guru mājhe — I stay among the elders; heri go nayane — I see with the eyes; bayāna paṛiche mane — the face comes to mind; nibārite cāi — I want to hold back; nāhi nibāraṇa — there is no holding back; bikala karila prāṇe — He has troubled the soul

2.4Sitting among the elders, I see Him with my eyes, His face comes to my mind;
I try to hold myself back — I cannot: He has thrown my soul into turmoil.

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের নিছনি লইয়া সকলি ছাড়িয়া দিব ।
লোচনের মনে হয় রাত্রি দিনে হিয়ার মাঝারে থোব ॥

gaurāṅgacām̐dera nichani laiyā sakali chāṛiyā diba |
locanera mane haya rātri dine hiyāra mājhāre thoba ||

gaurāṅgacām̐dera nichani laiyā — giving myself away for Gaurangachand; sakali chāṛiyā diba — I will leave everything; locanera mane haya — it is on Lochana's mind; rātri dine — night and day; hiyāra mājhāre thoba — I will place [Him] in the heart

2.5Giving myself away for Gaurangachand, I will leave everything.
On Lochana's mind night and day: "I will place Him in my heart."

witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). amazement at His beauty. family, dharma and custom" is a motif of the padas on the gopis (Bhag. 10.29) transferred to the townswomen of Nadia; it is this transfer that the tradition rejects (introductory note; cf. chapter 27, note 43).

3. Lochana Dasa — "hiyāra mājhāre gaurāṅga rākhiyā…" (GPT1 p. 178, no. 64)

Nagari-bhava (only in the address to a friend). Having placed Gauranga in her heart, the townswoman will sit in solitude and look at the moon of His face; she has heard that He who was formerly in Gokula, in Nanda's house, has now appeared in Navadvipa, in Shachi's house. Raga kamoda.8

হিয়ার মাঝারে গৌরাঙ্গ রাখিয়া বিরলে বসিয়া রব ।
মনের সাধে ও মুখচাঁদে নয়নে নয়নে থোব ॥

hiyāra mājhāre gaurāṅga rākhiyā birale basiyā raba |
manera sādhe o mukhacām̐de nayane nayane thoba ||

hiyāra mājhāre — in the heart; gaurāṅga rākhiyā — placing Gauranga; birale basiyā raba — I will sit in solitude; manera sādhe — to my heart's content; o mukha-cām̐de — that moon of a face; nayane nayane thoba — I will keep before my eyes

3.1Having placed Gauranga in my heart, I will sit in solitude;
to my heart's content I will keep that moon of a face before my eyes.

শুনেছি পূরবে গোকুলনগরে নন্দের মন্দিরে যে ।
নবদ্বীপ আসি হৈলা পরকাশি শচীর মন্দিরে সে ॥

śunechi pūrabe gokulanagare nandera mandire ye |
nabadvīpa āsi hailā parakāśi śacīra mandire se ||

śunechi — I have heard; pūrabe — formerly; gokula-nagare — in Gokula; nandera mandire ye — He who [was] in Nanda's house; nabadvīpa āsi — coming to Navadvipa; hailā parakāśi — revealed Himself; śacīra mandire se — He, in Shachi's house

3.2I have heard: He who formerly [was] in Gokula, in the house of Nanda, —
He has come to Navadvipa and revealed Himself in the house of Shachi.9

লোচনের বাণী শুন গো সজনি কি আর বলিব তোরে ।
হেরিয়া বদন ভুলে গেল মন পাসরিতে নারি তারে ॥

locanera bāṇī śuna go sajani ki āra baliba tore |
heriyā badana bhule gela mana pāsarite nāri tāre ||

locanera bāṇī — the word of Lochana; śuna go sajani — listen, friend; ki āra baliba tore — what more shall I tell you; heriyā badana — seeing the face; bhule gela mana — the mind forgot itself; pāsarite nāri tāre — I cannot forget Him

3.3The word of Lochana: listen, friend, what more shall I tell you?
I saw the face — and the mind forgot itself: I cannot forget Him.

witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. The nagari motif is only in the address "friend": in substance this is a praise of Gaura and contemplation of Him in the heart. On
nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27).
Chaitanya-mangala.

4. Lochana Dasa — "gaurāṅgabadane harila cetane…" (GPT1 p. 178, no. 65)

Nagari-bhava. Gauranga's face has stolen the townswoman's reason: she wants to forget — she cannot. Refrain: "Gora has entered the heart; the townswomen of Nadia have gone mad — I have understood it by myself." Seeing Gauranga's feet, a noble wife leaves her husband; whether it is righteous or not — it is shameful even to say. Raga kamoda.10

গৌরাঙ্গবদনে হরিল চেতনে বড় পরমাদ দেখি ।
পাসরিতে চাই পাসরা না যায় উপায় বল গো সখি ॥

gaurāṅgabadane harila cetane baṛa paramāda dekhi |
pāsarite cāi pāsarā nā yāya upāya bala go sakhi ||

gaurāṅga-badane — Gauranga's face; harila cetane — stole the reason; baṛa paramāda dekhi — I see a great calamity; pāsarite cāi — I want to forget; pāsarā nā yāya — it cannot be forgotten; upāya bala go sakhi — tell me a way, friend

4.1Gauranga's face has stolen my reason — I see a great calamity has come;
I want to forget — I cannot forget; tell me, friend, what am I to do?

গোরা পশিল হিয়ার মাঝে ।
নদীয়া-নাগরী হইল পাগলী বুঝিনু আপন কাজে ॥

gorā paśila hiyāra mājhe |
nadīyā-nāgarī haila pāgalī bujhinu āpana kāje ||

gorā paśila hiyāra mājhe — Gora entered the heart; nadīyā-nāgarī — the townswomen of Nadia; haila pāgalī — went mad; bujhinu āpana kāje — I understood by my own case

4.2(Refrain) Gora has entered the heart.
The townswomen of Nadia have gone mad — I have understood it by myself.

যখন দেখিনু গৌরাঙ্গচরণ তখনি হরিল মন ।
কুলবতী সতী যুবতী যেজন ত্যজে নিজ পতিধন ॥

yakhana dekhinu gaurāṅgacaraṇa takhani harila mana |
kulabatī satī yubatī yejana tyaje nija patidhana ||

yakhana dekhinu — when I saw; gaurāṅga-caraṇa — Gauranga's feet; takhani harila mana — at once He stole the mind; kulabatī satī yubatī yejana — whatever young noble faithful wife; tyaje nija pati-dhana — leaves her own treasure, the husband

4.3As soon as I saw Gauranga's feet, He at once stole my mind;
a young noble faithful wife, whoever she may be, leaves her treasure — her husband.11

না জানি ধরমে কি জানি করমে কহিতে বাসি হে লাজ ।
লোচনদাসের মন বেয়াকুল এবে সে বুঝিল কাজ ॥

nā jāni dharame ki jāni karame kahite bāsi he lāja |
locanadāsera mana beyākula ebe se bujhila kāja ||

nā jāni dharame — I do not know if by dharma; ki jāni karame — or by karma; kahite bāsi he lāja — I am ashamed to say; locana-dāsera mana beyākula — Lochana Dasa's mind is troubled; ebe se bujhila kāja — now he has understood the matter

4.4I do not know whether by dharma or by karma — I am ashamed even to say;
Lochana Dasa is troubled in soul: now he too has understood what it is.

witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). Nadia (see note 7); translated exactly. "Whether by dharma or by karma" (4.4) — i.e., one cannot tell whether it is righteous or sinful. In 4.4b the poet speaks of himself in the third person: he too has "understood by himself" the power of Gaura's form (cf. the refrain).

5. Lochana Dasa — "(gaurera) rūpa lāgi ām̐khi jhore…" (GPT1 pp. 179–180, no. 67)

Nagari-bhava. The townswoman's eyes weep for Gaura's form, each of her limbs for each of His; why did she go to the Suradhuni, why did she look at Gaura — He pierced her with the arrows of His eyes; her eyes want to go and look, her mind wants to become His maidservant; her mind slipped on the slippery ghat of the ocean of His beauty. She will cut open her breast and hide Him there together with her life. Raga "yatharaga".12

(গৌরের) রূপ লাগি আঁখি ঝোরে গুণে মন ভোর ।

(gaurera) rūpa lāgi ām̐khi jhore guṇe mana bhora |
prati aṅga lāgi kām̐de prati aṅga mora ||

(gaurera) — (of Gaura); rūpa lāgi — for the form; ām̐khi jhore — the eyes weep; guṇe mana bhora — the mind is enraptured by the virtues; prati aṅga lāgi — for each limb; kām̐de prati aṅga mora — each of my limbs weeps

for each [of His] limbs each of my limbs weeps.

হিয়ার পরশ লাগি হিয়া মোর কাঁদে ।
পরাণ পুতলী মোর হিয়া নাহি বাঁধে ॥

hiyāra paraśa lāgi hiyā mora kām̐de |
parāṇa putalī mora hiyā nāhi bām̐dhe ||

hiyāra paraśa lāgi — for the touch of the breast; hiyā mora kām̐de — my breast weeps; parāṇa putalī mora — the darling doll of my soul; hiyā nāhi bām̐dhe — the heart cannot hold

5.2For the touch of [His] breast my breast weeps;
my heart cannot hold the darling doll of my soul.13

আমি কেন সুরধুনী গেলাম (গেলাম ! গেলাম !!) ।
কেন গৌররূপে নয়ন দিলাম ॥

kena gaurarūpe nayana dilāma ||

āmi kena suradhunī gelāma — why did I go to the Suradhuni; (gelāma gelāma) — (I went! I went!); kena gaura-rūpe nayana dilāma — why did I turn my eyes to Gaura's form

5.3Why did I go to the Suradhuni (I went! I went!!),
why did I turn my eyes to the form of Gaura?

আমি কেনই চাইলাম গৌরপানে ।
(গৌর) আমায় হান্‌লে দুটী নয়ন-বাণে ॥

āmi kenai cāilāma gaurapāne |
(gaura) āmāya hānle duṭī nayana-bāṇe ||

āmi kenai cāilāma gaura-pāne — why ever did I look at Gaura; (gaura) — (Gaura); āmāya hānle — pierced me; duṭī nayana-bāṇe — with the two arrows of His eyes

5.4Why ever did I look at Gaura?
(Gaura) pierced me with the two arrows of His eyes.

আমার নয়ন বোলে ওরূপ দেখে আসি ।
আমার মন বলে তার হৈগা দাসী ॥

āmāra mana bale tāra haigā dāsī ||

āmāra nayana bole — my eyes say; o-rūpa dekhe āsi — let us go and see that form; āmāra mana bale — my mind says; tāra haigā dāsī — I will become His maidservant

5.5My eyes say: "Let us go and look at that form";
my mind says: "I will become His maidservant."

করে নয়ন-পথে আনাগোনা ।
আমার পাঁজর কেটে করল খানা ॥

kare nayana-pathe ānāgonā |
āmāra pām̐jara keṭe karala khānā ||

kare nayana-pathe ānāgonā — He comes and goes by the path of the eyes; āmāra pām̐jara keṭe — cutting through my ribs; karala khānā — made a dwelling (or: cut to pieces)

5.6He comes and goes by the path of the eyes;
He has cut through my ribs and made Himself a dwelling [there].14

গৌররূপ-সাগরের পিছল ঘাটে ।
আমার মন গিয়া তায় পড়ল ছুটে ॥

gaurarūpa-sāgarera pichala ghāṭe |
āmāra mana giyā tāya paṛala chuṭe ||

gaura-rūpa-sāgarera — of the ocean of Gaura's form; pichala ghāṭe — at the slippery ghat; āmāra mana giyā tāya — my mind, going there; paṛala chuṭe — slipped and fell

5.7At the slippery ghat of the ocean that is Gaura's form
my mind went down, slipped and fell.

একে গৌররূপ তায় পীরিত মাখা ।
(তাতে আবার) ঈষৎ হাসি নয়ন বাঁকা ॥

eke gaurarūpa tāya pīrita mākhā |
(tāte ābāra) īṣat hāsi nayana bām̐kā ||

eke gaura-rūpa — as if Gaura's form were not enough; tāya pīrita mākhā — it is steeped in love besides; (tāte ābāra) — (and on top of that); īṣat hāsi — a slight smile; nayana bām̐kā — a sidelong glance

5.8As if Gaura's form were not enough — it is steeped in love besides,
(and on top of that) a slight smile and a sidelong glance.

(গৌরের) যত রূপ তত বেশ ।
ও ! সে ! ভাজিতে পাঁজর শেষ ॥

(gaurera) yata rūpa tata beśa |
o ! se ! bhājite pām̐jara śeṣa ||

(gaurera) — (Gaura has); yata rūpa tata beśa — as many forms as adornments; o se — oh, He; bhājite — scorching (lit. frying); pām̐jara śeṣa — the ribs are spent

5.9(Gaura has) as many forms as He has adornments;
oh! He! — He scorches me till my ribs are spent.15

(গৌরের) রূপ লাগি আঁখি ঝোরে ।
গুণে মনোভোর করে ॥

(gaurera) rūpa lāgi ām̐khi jhore |
guṇe manobhora kare ||

(gaurera) rūpa lāgi — for the form (of Gaura); ām̐khi jhore — the eyes weep; guṇe mano-bhora kare — the virtues enrapture the mind

5.10For the form (of Gaura) my eyes weep;
His virtues intoxicate my mind.

(গৌররূপ) তিল আধ পাসরিতে নারি ।
কি খনে (গৌরাঙ্গরূপ) হিয়ার মাঝে ধরি ॥

(gaurarūpa) tila ādha pāsarite nāri |
ki khane (gaurāṅgarūpa) hiyāra mājhe dhari ||

(gaura-rūpa) — (Gaura's form); tila ādha pāsarite nāri — I cannot forget for half a moment; ki khane — in what an hour; (gaurāṅga-rūpa) — (Gauranga's form); hiyāra mājhe dhari — I placed in my heart

5.11Not for a moment can I forget (Gaura's form);
in what an hour did I place (Gauranga's form) in my heart!

এ বুক চিরিয়া রাখি পরাণেরই সঙ্গ ।
মনে হোলে বাহির ক'রে দেখি মুখচন্দ ॥

e buka ciriyā rākhi parāṇerai saṅga |
mane hole bāhira ka're dekhi mukhacanda ||

e buka ciriyā rākhi — I will cut open this breast and keep [Him]; parāṇerai saṅga — together with my very life; mane hole — when I wish; bāhira ka're dekhi — I take Him out and look; mukha-canda — the moon of the face

5.12I will cut open this breast and hide [Him] there together with my very life;
when I wish, I will take Him out and look at the moon of His face.16

গৌররূপ হেরি সবার অন্তর উল্লাস ।
আনন্দ হৃদয়ে কহে এ লোচন দাস ॥

gaurarūpa heri sabāra antara ullāsa |
ānanda hṛdaye kahe e locana dāsa ||

gaura-rūpa heri — seeing Gaura's form; sabāra antara ullāsa — everyone's heart rejoices; ānanda hṛdaye — with joy in the heart; kahe e locana dāsa — says this Lochana Dasa

5.13At the sight of Gaura's form everyone's heart rejoices;
with joy in his heart says this Lochana Dasa.

two couplets (5.1–5.2) are the beginning of Jnanadasa's pada PK 748 "rūpa lāgi ām̐khi jhure guṇe mana bhora…" (PK vol. 2, 8th pallava, signature "jñāna"; also in the Padamrita-samudra), where Radha weeps for Shyama; here "(gaurera)" — "of Gaura" — is added, and the whole pada is turned to Gaura; from then on it is colloquial Bengali. Developing the opening lines of a well-known pada is a usual practice of kirtaniyas; the pada is a composite, and its attribution to Lochana rests only on the signature in GPT (C). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). the kirtana singers (akhar), as GPT prints them; they are translated in brackets. "The darling doll of my soul" (parāṇa putalī) — what is dearest; PK 748 has here "parāṇa pirīti lāgi," while "parāṇa-putalī mora" is the reading of MS P-R-Sa in the PK apparatus: GPT follows it.

6. Lochana Dasa — "uṣaḥkāle sakhī mile jala bharite yāya…" (GPT1 pp. 180–181, no. 68)

Nagari-bhava. At dawn a young wife goes with her friends for water and meets Gora with His friends on the road; having filled her pitcher, she stands as if stunned and gazes: who is this — a god of rasa? Brows, eyes, nose, teeth, the colour of His body, arms, necklace, white cloth, ringing anklets; the nagara of beauty has risen — and the mind of "the nagari Lochana" is swept away. Raga "yatharaga".17

উষঃকালে সখী মিলে জল ভরিতে যায় ।
সঙ্গে সখা পথে দেখা হলো গোরারায় ॥

uṣaḥkāle sakhī mile jala bharite yāya |
saṅge sakhā pathe dekhā halo gorārāya ||

uṣaḥkāle — at dawn; sakhī mile — together with friends; jala bharite yāya — she goes to fetch water; saṅge sakhā — with [His] friends; pathe dekhā halo — on the road there was a meeting; gorārāya — Gora-raya

on the road — a meeting: Gora-raya with His friends.

মরমে মরি কলসি ভরি তুলে নিলাম কাঁখে ।
থাকিত পারা চৌউর হারা বঁধু দাঁড়ায়ে দেখে ॥

marame mari kalasi bhari tule nilāma kām̐khe |
thākita pārā cauura hārā bam̐dhu dām̐ṛāye dekhe ||

marame mari — dying at heart; kalasi bhari — filling the pitcher; tule nilāma kām̐khe — I lifted it onto my hip; thākita pārā — as if stunned; cauura hārā — beside herself (?); bam̐dhu (= badhū) — the young wife; dām̐ṛāye dekhe — stands and gazes

6.2Dying at heart, I filled the pitcher and lifted it onto my hip;
the young wife stands as if stunned, beside herself, and gazes.18

ওবা কে রসের দে রূপের সীমা নাই ।
কোন বিধি রসের নিধি কৈল এক ঠাঁই ॥

obā ke rasera de rūpera sīmā nāi |
kona bidhi rasera nidhi kaila eka ṭhām̐i ||

obā ke — who is this; rasera de — a god (?) of rasa; rūpera sīmā nāi — there is no limit to the beauty; kona bidhi — what creator; rasera nidhi — the treasure of rasa; kaila eka ṭhām̐i — gathered in one place

6.3"Who is this — a god of rasa? there is no limit to His beauty;
what creator has gathered the treasure of rasa in one place?

যুগ্মভুরু কামের গুরু ছাড়ছে ফুলের বাণ ।
কেমন কালি ধরে তুলি ক'রেছে নির্ম্মাণ ॥

yugmabhuru kāmera guru chāṛache phulera bāṇa |
kemana kāli dhare tuli ka'reche nirmmāṇa ||

yugma-bhuru — the pair of brows; kāmera guru — the teacher of Kama; chāṛche phulera bāṇa — shoots flower-arrows; kemana kāli — with what ink; dhare tuli — holding a brush; kareche nirmmāṇa — they were made

6.4The pair of brows — the teacher of Kama — shoots flower-arrows;
with what ink, with what brush were they made?

আঁখির তল নিরমল নীল-কমলের দল ।
অরুণতা দুটী পাতা ক'রছে ছলছল্ ॥

ām̐khira tala niramala nīla-kamalera dala |
aruṇatā duṭī pātā ka'rache chalachal ||

ām̐khira tala — the depths of the eyes; niramala — spotless; nīla-kamalera dala — petals of a blue lotus; aruṇatā duṭī pātā — two reddish lids; karche chalachala — glisten moist

6.5The depths of the eyes are spotless petals of a blue lotus;
the two lids, reddish, glisten moist.

তিলফুল কিসে তুল এমনি নাসার শোভা ।
কুঁদে কাটি পরিপাটী কিবা দন্তের আভা ॥

tilaphula kise tula emani nāsāra śobhā |
kum̐de kāṭi paripāṭī kibā dantera ābhā ||

tila-phula — a sesame flower; kise tula — how could it compare; emani nāsāra śobhā — such is the beauty of the nose; kum̐de kāṭi — turned on a lathe; paripāṭī — even; kibā dantera ābhā — what a lustre of teeth

6.6A sesame flower — how could it compare? such is the beauty of the nose;
turned on a lathe, even — what a lustre of teeth!

হিঙ্গুল ভালে হরিতালে নবনী দিল ভেঁজে ।
কাঁচা সোণা চাঁদখানা রসান দিল মেজে ॥

hiṅgula bhāle haritāle nabanī dila bhem̐je |
kām̐cā soṇā cām̐dakhānā rasāna dila meje ||

hiṅgula bhāle haritāle — vermilion and orpiment; nabanī dila bhem̐je — kneaded with fresh butter; kām̐cā soṇā — pure gold; cām̐dakhānā — the moon; rasāna dila meje — laid on and burnished

6.7Vermilion and orpiment were kneaded with fresh butter;
pure gold, the moon — laid on and burnished.

আল্‌তা তুলি দুধে গুলি কর দিয়াছে ছেনে ।
চাঁদকে আনি ছানি ছানি তায় বসালে জেনে ॥

āltā tuli dudhe guli kara diyāche chene |
cām̐dake āni chāni chāni tāya basāle jene ||

āltā tuli — taking lac-dye; dudhe guli — dissolving in milk; kara diyāche chene — they moulded the hands; cām̐dake āni — bringing the moon; chāni chāni — sifting and sifting; tāya basāle jene — skilfully set it there

6.8Dissolving lac-dye in milk, they moulded the hands;
they brought the moon, sifted it and sifted it — and skilfully set it there.19

গলে হার শোভে তার কিবা বাহুর ভাতি ।
গগন হতে জল তুলতে নামল সোণার হাতী ॥

gale hāra śobhe tāra kibā bāhura bhāti |
gagana hate jala tulate nāmala soṇāra hātī ||

gale hāra — a necklace on the neck; śobhe tāra — shines on Him; kibā bāhura bhāti — what a splendour of the arms; gagana hate — from the sky; jala tulte — to draw water; nāmala soṇāra hātī — a golden elephant came down

6.9On His neck a necklace — how it shines! and what a splendour of arms! —
as if a golden elephant had come down from the sky to draw water.

কটি আঁটি পরিপাটী ধবল বসন সাজে ।
সুললিত ভুবনজিত পায়ে নূপুর বাজে ॥

kaṭi ām̐ṭi paripāṭī dhabala basana sāje |
sulalita bhubanajita pāye nūpura bāje ||

kaṭi ām̐ṭi — girt at the waist; paripāṭī — neatly; dhabala basana sāje — the white cloth adorns; sulalita — graceful; bhubana-jita — conquering the world; pāye nūpura bāje — anklets ring on the feet

6.10Neatly girt, the white cloth adorns Him;
graceful, conquering the world, the anklets ring on His feet.

রূপের নাগর রসের সাগর উদয় হলো এসে ।
নাগরী লোচনের মন তাইতে গেলো ভেসে ॥

rūpera nāgara rasera sāgara udaya halo ese |
nāgarī locanera mana tāite gelo bhese ||

rūpera nāgara — the nagara of beauty; rasera sāgara — the ocean of rasa; udaya halo ese — has come and risen; nāgarī locanera mana — the mind of the nagari Lochana; tāite gelo bhese — by this was swept away

6.11The nagara of beauty, the ocean of rasa, has come and risen [like the sun];
by this the mind of the nagari Lochana has been swept away."20

witnesses; attribution by GPT only — C. The pada begins as a narrative in the third person ("goes") and passes into the first ("I filled"); so in the original. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). "young wife": the speaker about herself. "Beside herself" (cauura hārā) — the meaning is conjectural. "Friends" (sakhā) — the Lord's associates. colour of the body is a mixture of vermilion, orpiment and butter burnished like pure gold; "the moon sifted and set" in the hands is apparently the nails (cf. "the moons of the nails"). "A god of rasa" (rasera de) is conjectural (de = deba). tradition does not accept such worship of Gaura (introductory note). "The nagara of beauty" is an epithet of Gaura in nagari-bhava (ibid.).

শচীর গোরা কামের কোড়া দেখলাম ঘাটের কূলে ।
চাঁচর চুলে বেড়িয়া ভালে নব-মালতীর মালে ॥

(এমন) চিতচোরা মনোহরা নাইকো অবনীতে ॥

kām̐cā soṇā lāge ghṛṇā rūpera tulanā dite |
(emana) citacorā manoharā nāiko abanīte ||

kām̐cā soṇā — pure gold; lāge ghṛṇā — it is distasteful; rūpera tulanā dite — to compare with the beauty; (emana) — (such); cita-corā — a thief of hearts; manoharā — a charmer of minds; nāiko abanīte — there is not on earth

কি আর বলিছ গো সই (তোমায়) বুঝাব কি ।
(ছাদে) স্নানে যেতে সখীর সাথে গৌর দেখেছি ॥

(chāde) snāne yete sakhīra sāthe gaura dekhechi ||

ki āra balicha go sai — what more are you saying, friend; (tomāya) — (to you); bujhāba ki — how shall I explain; (chāde) — (on the roof?); snāne yete — going to bathe; sakhīra sāthe — with friends; gaura dekhechi — I saw Gaura

(সে) রূপ দেখি দুটী আঁখি ফিরাইতে নারি ।
পুনঃ তারে দেখবার তরে কতো সাধ করি ॥

(se) rūpa dekhi duṭī ām̐khi phirāite nāri |
punaḥ tāre dekhabāra tare kato sādha kari ||

(se) rūpa dekhi — seeing (that) form; duṭī ām̐khi phirāite nāri — I cannot turn my two eyes away; punaḥ tāre — Him again; dekhvāra tare — in order to see; kato sādha kari — how I long

Summary of Chapter 34

Chapter 34 completes the nagari padas of Lochana Dasa: of the 26 padas with his signature in section 3.2 of GPT, 22 are translated here (nos. 62–65, 67–79, 81–83, 85, 116; records pad-0735…0756); nos. 61 and 66 (= PK 2178, 2174) were translated in chapter 28; no. 80 (= PK 2088) is a passage of the Chaitanya-mangala (Madhya-khanda, part 4, vv. 110–118), no. 84 (= PK 777) is a pada of Vasu Ghosha (chapter 27, no. 16; in GPT1 it stands twice — as no. 17 with Vasu's signature and as no. 84 with Lochana's). All 22 padas are known only from GPT (nos. 16, 17 also from PVP, 1922, with the same signature); all are C: attribution by GPT only (the signature of a recognized author, but without independent witnesses; PVP, 1922, is a late anthology); no. 5 begins with two couplets of Jnanadasa's pada PK 748. In content: the purvaraga and anuraga of the townswomen (nos. 1–2, 4–10, 12–13, 15, 19–21); an imagined meeting and dreams with the motif of sambhoga (no. 1 — a fancy beside her husband; nos. 11, 18 — dreams); praise of Gaura's form and dance, where the nagari motif is only in the frame or the address (nos. 3, 14, 16) or absent in content (nos. 17, 22). Separate notes on attraction and sambhoga — 3, 26, 31, 33, 53; on the motif of "leaving family and husband" — 7, 11, 36, 45; on the Lord's looking at women — 26, 46, 56. Many of Lochana's padas end with a turn inward — "go into your own house, hold Gora in your heart" (nos. 11, 13, 20; cf. nos. 3, 22), and in several the teaching is voiced directly: Gaura is the same Krishna, "straightened" by Radha's love (16.4); His form is beyond prakriti (17.2); He has come in the guise of a devotee, covered with Radha's form (22.3). Doubtful places: the meaning of a number of colloquial words (5.6, 5.9, 6.2, 6.3, 7.1, 7.3, 13.8, 15.5, 18.5, 20.7, 22.4) — translated conjecturally, with notes; line 12.5 has no pair (lost in GPT).

Concluding Note to the Section of Nagari Padas (Chapters 27–34)

1. How many and whose. The section contains 183 padas in eight chapters: Vasu Ghosha — 40 (chapter 27 — 25 padas from PK; chapter 28 — 15 padas known from GPT); Nayanananda — 5; Yadunandana — 6 (the cycle of the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara, chapter 29; one signed "Yadu"); Yadu — 2; Murari — 2 (Murari Gupta by the GPT signature and Dasa Murari); Balarama Dasa — 1; Chandrashekhara — 1; Lochana Dasa — 24 (two padas from PK in chapter 28 and 22 from GPT in chapter 34); "Narahari" — 102 (chapters 29–33; nearly all by Narahari Chakravarti; their concluding note is at the end of chapter 33).

2. Attribution (scale — see the preface). A — 30: 26 padas of Vasu Ghosha (25 from PK and one confirmed by the Kshanada-gita-chintamani) and 4 padas of Nayanananda from PK. B — 90: "probably Chakravarti" — 81 (75 found in the Gaura-charita-chintamani, 6 only in the Bhakti-ratnakara), Yadunandana — 6, Lochana Dasa — 2 (padas from PK, chapter 28), Vasu — 1 (GPT and the Gita-chandrodaya). C — 62: Lochana Dasa — 22 (chapter 34: signature only in GPT, without independent witnesses — "attribution by GPT only"), "Narahari" — 21 (padas only from GPT; some stand in place of the lost pages of GCC), Vasu — 12 (GPT only), Nayanananda — 1, Yadu — 2, Murari — 2, Balarama — 1, Chandrashekhara — 1. D — 1 (a pada signed Vasu, according to Majumdar a reworking of a pada on Krishna; chapter 28, no. 13). The earliest and most reliable layer is the padas of Vasu Ghosha and Nayanananda from the Padakalpataru; the rest is a poetic development of the nagari motif: Lochana Dasa (a disciple of Narahari Sarakara), Yadunandana (a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa) and, most of all, Narahari Chakravarti (first half of the eighteenth century).

3. Who speaks. In the great majority of padas the townswomen of Nadia speak — to a friend, to themselves, to the elders; in 25 "Narahari" padas (GPT 3.2 nos. 158–180 and 3.1 nos. 129–130 = GCC, kiranas 10–11) heavenly women speak, who only look at Nadia from the sky; in a few, the poet himself, putting himself in a townswoman's place ("the nagari Lochana," 34/6.11) or looking on from outside (34/15.11–15.13). Not nagari-bhava in content — 6 padas: Gaura's words in sleep in the words of Krishna (31/1), the heavenly women's replies praising the Lord's strictness (32/19–20, 33/3), Lochana's praise of Gaura's form (34/17, 22); in a number of other padas the nagari motif is only the address "friend" or the frame (28/1, 34/3, 14, 16 and others). Three padas are laments after the Lord's sannyasa (in 28/15 the speaker is probably Vishnupriya — then it is a lament of separation, not nagari-bhava), four are the women's words at His wedding.

4. What the corpus shows. The nagari padas speak of Gaura in the language of purvaraga and anuraga from the padas on Radha and the gopis: deceiving the elders, "leaving family and husband," dreams of a meeting. The later the layer, the more outspoken the motif: in Vasu Ghosha (PK) it is mostly admiration and longing; in the "Narahari" padas from GCC and in Lochana's colloquial padas — dreams with embraces and direct words of attraction. Yet even in them Gaura in the lila itself does not respond to attraction: He passes by, dances in kirtana, leans on His associates; the "meeting" happens only in the heroine's dream and fancy; in Narahari Chakravarti the Lord turns away and hurries off, and Lochana ends many padas with a call to "go into your own house" and keep Gora in the heart and voices the teaching directly (34/16.4, 17.2, 22.3).

5. The position of the tradition (briefly). The Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of the nagaris. Vrindavana Dasa (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi-khanda) testifies that the Lord in this incarnation did not look at any woman and that the wise do not glorify Him as "Gauranga-nagara"; Krishnadasa Kaviraja (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 1.5–6; Adi 4) reveals that Gaura is Krishna Himself in the bhava and radiance of Radha, who came to taste Her love as a devotee, not as an enjoying hero; Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati counts "gaura-nagari" among the apasampradayas — and, publishing Lochana's Chaitanya-mangala, refuses to ascribe this doctrine to it. The nagari padas have been translated for the completeness of the corpus of padas on Gaura and as a historical document — faithfully to the author, without worldly vocabulary beyond the original and without softening, with notes on the position of the tradition; they are not a basis for worshipping Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27).
